previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___, a man with secondary progressive multiple sclerosis and neurogenic bladder managed with a chronic Foley catheter, was admitted for weakness, diarrhea, and hematuria. He presented with sepsis from a catheter-associated urinary tract infection, with labs showing leukocytosis, hemoconcentration, and acute kidney injury. He was treated in the ICU with fluid resuscitation and broad-spectrum antibiotics—cefepime and vancomycin—which were continued for 14 days. His hospital course was complicated by a lower gastrointestinal bleed from proctitis, requiring blood transfusions, and hospital-acquired pneumonia, which resolved with treatment. He also developed ileus and severe constipation, managed with disimpaction and a bowel regimen. His oxybutynin was discontinued due to contributing to tachycardia and dry mouth. He improved clinically, with resolution of infection, stabilization of hemoglobin, and return of bowel function. He was discharged home with home health services, a new Foley catheter, and instructions to continue methenamine and vitamin C for UTI prophylaxis, along with a bowel regimen and follow-up for colonoscopy and urology evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ h/o MS, neurogenic bladder s/p multiple drug resistant UTIs 
presents with pyelonephritis.

# UTI: Patient with fever and grossly positive UA in ED (>182 
WBC and RBC) was started empirically on vancomycin and cefepime 
pending urine culture and sensitivity, given history of 
Pseudomonas and Staph Aureus UTIs in the past. Urine culture 
results then showed resistance to most cephalosporins so patient 
was started on Unasyn pending results of an add on test for 
cefepime. Urine culture subsequently subsequently confirmed that 
the E. Coli was Cefepime sensitive and patient was transitioned 
back to Cefepime as patient was refusing placement in a long 
term care facility and would require ___ for IV antibiotics.  
PICC placement was attempted at bedside by IV team, however 
there was difficulty advancing a guidewire, the PICC was placed 
by ___ on ___ and appropriate placement was confirmed 
radiographically. The patient was discharged home on IV Cefepime 
with plan to complete a 14 day course on ___.

# Bladder calculi: patient with CT Abdomen and pelvis on ___ 
showing calculi in the bladder. Given recurrent UTIs it is 
likely that these calculi have become infected. Discussed with 
urology and plan made for removal of bladder calculi as an 
outpatient. Patient will be seen in clinic by Dr. ___ on 
___ to plan for calculi removal.

# Self Care: On presentation to the ED the patient was noted to 
be covered in stool and have stool soilage of his foley catheter 
insertion site. The patient stated that he had not had his foley 
changed since his last admission for UTI approximately 3 weeks 
prior to presentation. Patient was encouraged to consider 
placement in a long term care facility, however he refused to 
consider placement. Plan was made for patient to go home with 
___ and have weekly foley changes at home to prevent further 
UTIs.

# Multiple Sclerosis: was noted to have diffuse weakness and 
spacticity. No steroids during admission due to acute infection.

radiology_notes.text:
PICC LINE PLACEMENT.

INDICATION:  IV access needed for antibiotics.

The procedure was explained to the patient.  A timeout was performed.

RADIOLOGIST:  Dr. ___ Dr. ___ the procedure.

TECHNIQUE:  Using sterile technique and local anesthesia, the right basilic
vein was punctured under direct ultrasound guidance using a micropuncture set.
Hard copies of ultrasound images were obtained before and immediately after
establishing intravenous access.  A peel-away sheath was then placed over a
guidewire and a single-lumen PICC line measuring 44 cm in length was then
placed through the peel-away sheath with its tip positioned in the SVC under
fluoroscopic guidance.  Position of the catheter was confirmed by a
fluoroscopic spot film of the chest.

The peel-away sheath and guidewire were then removed.  The catheter was
secured to the skin, flushed, and a sterile dressing applied.

The patient tolerated the procedure well.  There were no immediate
complications.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated ultrasound and fluoroscopically guided 5 ___
single-lumen PICC line placement via the right basilic venous approach.  Final
internal length is 44 cm, with the tip positioned in SVC.  The line is ready
to use.
